subject: DocuSign deprecation / contract inbox migration plan
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DocuSign deprecation / contract inbox migration plan

Team —

Quick background: Legal Ops ran a discovery and confirmed DocuSign is scheduled to end-support one of our embedded signing workflows in Q1 2027 (see vendor note attached). We need a short, practical plan to either: (A) migrate all active contract signing and storage to Ironclad (recommended by Legal), or (B) adopt DocuSign's new API layer with the migration partner.

As a first step I want to scope out: cost delta, migration effort, gaps for SSO / audit logs / KMS integration, and any customer-facing risk windows. Can you each take the following and flag blockers by EOD Thursday?
- Marissa: confirm legal retention/chain-of-custody requirements and any clause changes we need in MSA and PO templates.
- Laura: procurement + SSO/KMS integration feasibility; estimate vendor negotiation levers (multi-year commit, marketplace credits).
- Nikhil: expected run-rate impact to billing (token storage, e-sign per-envelope costs) and any finance signoff steps.

I've attached the vendor deprecation notice and a rough cost comparison sheet that Marissa pushed earlier. We'll then pull in the vendor reps for a technical kickoff if we decide to proceed.

Attachments: redwood_docusign_decom_scope_v1.pdf; docusign_vs_ironclad_costs_2026Q4.xlsx

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DocuSign deprecation / contract inbox migration plan

Markus —

Acknowledged. Quick notes from Legal Ops after a first pass:
- Retention / e-discovery: we need immutable audit trails for executed contracts for 7 years (some enterprise accounts require 10). Any migration approach must preserve original signed PDFs and stamped audit trails.
- Chain-of-custody: Ironclad supports native storage and retention holds; DocuSign is proposing a "signed-asset export" but it's a separate paid addon and we need proof of parity.
- Contract language: add a short transition clause in renewals/AMCs giving us the right to migrate signed assets to a new provider with 30 days notice, and ensure embassy language for customers with strict residency requirements.

I pulled the cost sheet and will annotate with legal risk items and redlines on the MSA. I'll upload to Confluence later today. If we go Ironclad, expect ~3–4 weeks of Legal review for redlines.

Marissa
Sr. Manager, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@docusign.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: docusign-sales@docusign.com
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DocuSign deprecation / contract inbox migration plan

Hi Markus —

Thanks for the note and for sharing the deprecation advisory. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- The embedded signing API you're using is EOL but DocuSign has a migration path (Platform API v3) with a migration partner that can handle a lift-and-shift with preserved audit trails. There's an additional one-time migration fee that covers exported artifacts and validation.
- If you choose to stay on DocuSign, we can offer a 12-month transitional credit to offset migration partner costs (we can detail in SOW).
- On SSO/KMS: we support SAML + SCIM and integrate with major KMS providers; for BYOK/HSM you will need our enterprise tier.

I'll attach the preliminary SOW template and migration partner contact. Happy to join a call next week with your engineering and legal teams.

Attachments: docusign_migration_sow_template.pdf; migration_partner_contact.vcf

Best,
Sarah Kim
Enterprise Account Executive — DocuSign
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DocuSign deprecation / contract inbox migration plan

Folks —

High level finance take after reviewing the cost workbook: moving to Ironclad looks like a ~15–20% increase in annual platform spend on the baseline, but we get consolidated contract storage and fewer per-envelope transaction fees which reduces variability. Key items for decision:
- Upfront migration cost vs. recurring delta (spread over 3 years) — vendor credits matter.
- Tax / procurement impact if we buy via marketplace vs. direct (marketplace can simplify PO terms and provide credits).
- Any revenue-impact risk if this interrupts sales ops (signature downtime). We should schedule the migration in a weekend window and keep a fallback to DocuSign for 48 hours.

I added a short scenario table in the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_migration_docs (see "migration scenarios.xlsx").

Nikhil
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@docusign.com>, vendor-itops@thirdparty-integrators.com
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DocuSign deprecation / contract inbox migration plan

Thanks everyone for the quick turn. Summary / next steps: 
- Decision: we will pilot a targeted migration of 3 sales teams (Enterprise, Platform, and Renewals) to Ironclad for contract creation + storage, while keeping DocuSign as a fallback for historical envelopes.
- Action items:
  1) Marissa to publish required MSA clause updates and retention checklist by 11/09. (Attachment: migration_checklist.md)
  2) Laura to negotiate an Ironclad pilot price (90-day pilot) and secure an SSO/KMS test environment by 11/12.
  3) Nikhil to prepare cost-amortization scenarios and schedule a weekend migration window (target: Dec 10–12).
  4) Markus to coordinate vendor kickoff, confirm SOW with Sarah and the migration partner, and create a rollback plan.

We'll run a technical kickoff on Friday 11/05 at 09:00 PT (invite to follow). If anyone sees a blocker to the pilot approach please flag here — otherwise I'll start the vendor SOW process with Sarah today.

Thanks —
Markus
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
